functions.name: core_pad_output
functions.brief: Configure a pad as push-pull output (default).

functions.name: core_pad_output_od
functions.brief: Configure a pad as open-drain output with optional pull resistor. Use PULL_UP for a wired-AND / I2C-style bus, PULL_NONE for external pull.

functions.name: core_pad_input
functions.brief: Configure a pad as input with pull resistor.

functions.name: core_pad_write
functions.brief: Set a pad high (ON) or low (OFF).

functions.name: core_pad_read
functions.brief: Read a pad. Returns 0 or 1.

functions.name: core_pad_toggle
functions.brief: Toggle a pad output.

functions.name: core_pad_resolve
functions.brief: Resolve a pad to a fast handle once, outside the hot loop.

functions.name: core_pad_fast_set
functions.brief: Drive the resolved pad high — single BSRR write.

functions.name: core_pad_fast_clear
functions.brief: Drive the resolved pad low — single BSRR write.

functions.name: core_pad_fast_write
functions.brief: Drive the resolved pad to `state` (0/1) — single BSRR write.

functions.name: core_pad_fast_read
functions.brief: Read the resolved pad — single IDR load. Returns 0 or 1.

functions.name: core_pad_bulk_write
functions.signature: core_pad_bulk_write(GPIO_TypeDef * port, uint32_t set_mask, uint32_t clear_mask)
functions.brief: Bulk update many pins on ONE port in a single atomic BSRR write: pins in `set_mask` go high, pins in `clear_mask` go low (set wins on overlap, per BSRR). Build the masks from the generated PAD_n_MASK defines. Useful for synchronized buses / LED matrices without per-pad jitter.

functions.name: core_pad_analog
functions.brief: Configure a pad as analog (for ADC, DAC, comparator).

functions.name: core_pad_speed
functions.brief: Set the output speed (slew rate) of a pad. Use SPEED_LOW / SPEED_MED / SPEED_HIGH / SPEED_VHIGH. Only affects outputs — input pads ignore this setting.

functions.name: core_pad_on_change
functions.signature: core_pad_on_change(uint8_t pad, uint32_t edge, hal_callback_t cb, void * ctx)
functions.brief: Register an edge-triggered callback on a pad. The pad is automatically configured as input with a sensible pull resistor based on edge direction: rising  → pull-down (idle low) falling → pull-up   (idle high) both    → no pull   (external bias expected)

functions.name: core_pad_on_change_stop
functions.brief: Stop the interrupt on a pad.

functions.name: hal_pad_lookup
functions.brief: Look up the GPIO port and pin for a tile pad number. Returns {NULL, 0} for pads with no GPIO (power, reset, etc.).

functions.name: hal_pad_output
functions.brief: Configure a pad as push-pull output. Enables the port clock.

functions.name: hal_pad_output_od
functions.brief: Configure a pad as open-drain output with pull selection. Enables the port clock.

functions.name: hal_pad_input
functions.brief: Configure a pad as input with pull selection.

functions.name: hal_pad_analog
functions.brief: Configure a pad as analog (for ADC, DAC, comparator).

functions.name: hal_pad_af
functions.signature: hal_pad_af(uint8_t pad, uint32_t af, uint32_t otype, uint32_t speed, uint32_t pull)
functions.brief: Configure a pad for alternate function.

functions.name: hal_pad_write
functions.brief: Write a pad: 0 = low, non-zero = high

functions.name: hal_pad_read
functions.brief: Read a pad. Returns 0 or 1.

functions.name: hal_pad_toggle
functions.brief: Toggle a pad.

functions.name: hal_exti_enable
functions.signature: hal_exti_enable(uint8_t pad, uint32_t edge, hal_callback_t cb, void * ctx)
functions.brief: Enable an edge-triggered interrupt on a tile pad. Configures the pad's GPIO pin as an EXTI source, stores the callback, and enables the NVIC IRQ.  The pad must already be configured as an input (see hal_pad_input or tal_exti_enable which does this automatically).

params.name: cb
params.description: Function called from ISR context on each edge

functions.name: hal_exti_disable
functions.brief: Disable the EXTI interrupt on a tile pad. Clears the callback and disables the EXTI line.  The NVIC IRQ is only disabled when no other lines sharing the same IRQ are active (relevant for grouped IRQs on L0/L4).

functions.name: ll_gpio_set
functions.brief: Set one or more pins high (write 1s to BSRR lower half)

functions.name: ll_gpio_clear
functions.brief: Set one or more pins low (write 1s to BSRR upper half)

functions.name: ll_gpio_toggle
functions.brief: Toggle one or more pins (XOR with ODR)

functions.name: ll_gpio_read
functions.brief: Read the input state of one or more pins

functions.name: ll_gpio_read_output
functions.brief: Read the output state of one or more pins

functions.name: ll_gpio_set_mode
functions.signature: ll_gpio_set_mode(GPIO_TypeDef * port, uint32_t pin, uint32_t mode)
functions.brief: Set the mode for a single pin. mode: LL_GPIO_MODE_INPUT, _OUTPUT, _AF, or _ANALOG

functions.name: ll_gpio_set_output_type
functions.signature: ll_gpio_set_output_type(GPIO_TypeDef * port, uint32_t pin, uint32_t otype)
functions.brief: Set the output type for a single pin. otype: LL_GPIO_OTYPE_PP (push-pull) or LL_GPIO_OTYPE_OD (open-drain)

functions.name: ll_gpio_set_speed
functions.signature: ll_gpio_set_speed(GPIO_TypeDef * port, uint32_t pin, uint32_t speed)
functions.brief: Set the output speed for a single pin. speed: LL_GPIO_SPEED_LOW, _MED, _HIGH, or _VHIGH

functions.name: ll_gpio_set_pull
functions.signature: ll_gpio_set_pull(GPIO_TypeDef * port, uint32_t pin, uint32_t pull)
functions.brief: Set the pull-up/pull-down for a single pin. pull: LL_GPIO_PULL_NONE, _UP, or _DOWN

functions.name: ll_gpio_set_af
functions.signature: ll_gpio_set_af(GPIO_TypeDef * port, uint32_t pin, uint32_t af)
functions.brief: Set the alternate function for a single pin (0-15). Pins 0-7 use AFR[0] (AFRL), pins 8-15 use AFR[1] (AFRH).

functions.name: ll_gpio_config_output
functions.brief: Configure a pin as general-purpose output (push-pull, no pull, medium speed).

functions.name: ll_gpio_config_input
functions.signature: ll_gpio_config_input(GPIO_TypeDef * port, uint32_t pin, uint32_t pull)
functions.brief: Configure a pin as input with optional pull.

functions.name: ll_gpio_config_af
functions.signature: ll_gpio_config_af(GPIO_TypeDef * port, uint32_t pin, uint32_t af, uint32_t otype, uint32_t speed, uint32_t pull)
functions.brief: Configure a pin for an alternate function. af:    alternate function number (0-15) otype: LL_GPIO_OTYPE_PP or _OD speed: LL_GPIO_SPEED_LOW/MED/HIGH/VHIGH pull:  LL_GPIO_PULL_NONE/UP/DOWN

functions.name: ll_gpio_config_analog
functions.brief: Configure a pin as analog (disconnects from digital logic).

functions.name: ll_exti_gpio_config
functions.signature: ll_exti_gpio_config(GPIO_TypeDef * port, uint32_t pin, uint32_t edge)
functions.brief: Set up a GPIO pin as an interrupt source. port: GPIO port (GPIOA, GPIOB, ...) pin:  pin number (0-15) edge: LL_EXTI_RISING, LL_EXTI_FALLING, or LL_EXTI_BOTH After calling this, enable the appropriate NVIC IRQ: ll_nvic_enable_irq(EXTI0_IRQn); Then implement the ISR handler (e.g. EXTI0_IRQHandler).

functions.name: ll_exti_config
functions.brief: Configure an EXTI line for interrupt generation. line:  EXTI line (0-15) edge:  LL_EXTI_RISING, LL_EXTI_FALLING, or LL_EXTI_BOTH Prerequisites: - SYSCFG clock enabled - EXTI source selected via ll_exti_set_source() - GPIO pin configured as input - NVIC IRQ enabled after this call

functions.name: ll_exti_disable
functions.brief: Disable an EXTI line interrupt

functions.name: ll_exti_pending
functions.brief: Check if an EXTI line has a pending interrupt

functions.name: ll_exti_clear_pending
functions.brief: Clear the pending flag for an EXTI line (write 1 to clear)

functions.name: ll_exti_sw_trigger
functions.brief: Generate a software interrupt on an EXTI line

functions.name: ll_exti_set_source
functions.brief: Select which GPIO port drives a given EXTI line. line:       EXTI line number (0-15, matches pin number) port_index: 0=GPIOA, 1=GPIOB, 2=GPIOC, ... Example: ll_exti_set_source(6, 1) → EXTI6 from GPIOB pin 6
